- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:line 275 (first-pass guard arm): `if [ "${guard_cmp_status}" -eq 1 ] && [ -e "${local_path}" ]; then`; falls through to the copy block at lines 287-291 `if [ ! -f "${local_path}" ] || ! diff ... ; then cp "${claude_source_path}" "${local_path}"` | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The keep-existing check uses only `[ -e "${local_path}" ]`, which returns false for a dangling consumer symlink; execution falls through to the copy block, where GNU `cp` fails.
  WHY: The step runs under `set -euo pipefail`, so the non-zero `cp` aborts the entire sync step and the workflow fails.
- .github/workflows/update_workflows.yml:line 275 (first-pass guard arm) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The dangling-symlink path also skips the "differing twin" warning, so an operator tracing `::warning::claude-guard-sync:` lines never sees any signal that the file was skipped.
  WHY: Operators see a generic step failure with "not writing through dangling symlink" on stderr instead of the labelled `::warning::` emitted for other guard paths.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: The PR description's "Evidence (step 5)" lists "the behavioural test asserts that no UNREVIEWED content lands", "Existing consumer guards are kept while a twin differs, and each kept file logs a warning: asserted", and "Non-guard sync is unchanged: asserted". The contract that "a consumer that already has the file keeps it" applies to a dangling symlink at that file path: the symlink is a file the consumer "already has", the guard arm in the first pass promises to keep it (per the documented rule), and the second pass's `[ -e ] || [ -L ]` check explicitly treats symlinks as existing. The test suite must therefore exercise the dangling-consumer-symlink case in the first pass so the asymmetry cannot regress silently.
  Expected change site: tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py — the `test_claude_sync_takes_guard_files_from_the_reviewed_claude_tree` family. The existing `test_claude_sync_symlink_guard_twin_is_handled_by_the_reviewed_pass` only creates a symlink on the twin side; no fixture creates a dangling consumer symlink at a guard path, so the regression has no automated witness.
  Evidence of absence: The seven behavioural tests added in this PR (`tests/test_update_workflows_guardrails.py:374-548`) collectively cover guard-equal, guard-differs-kept, guard-differs-installed, guard-missing-from-`.claude/`, no-twin-tree, no-tree-at-all, and a symlink-twin case. None of them write a dangling symlink to the consumer side at a guard path and assert the keep-existing behaviour; `_run_claude_sync` (lines 322-365) writes regular files for the `local` dict and never symlinks. Without such a fixture, the first-pass `[ -e ]` regression goes undetected by the suite.
  SEVERITY: MAJOR
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
